keyframe_review.note: 10,739 km2 for 366-302, a block at 115.86-117.12 E, 38.55-40.10 N, north-east of Baoding. The page puts the state in Pingshan County (the tombs and the capital Lingshou, about 114 E), Zhengding County (Dongyuan) and the Baoding/Tang County wall; the Cliopatria block holds none of Lingshou, Zhengding or the wall (the zhao dossier checked the cells). The page gives no area ('such a small nation'; the capital walls enclose about 4,000 m by 4,500 m), so no infobox ratio can be made; the three discs make 89 grid cells against the Cliopatria block's 62, and the two share no cell. The state begins in 381, not 366: use new keyframe zhongshan_-381 for 381-306. Same shape as the wei dossier's Zhongshan core.

The Zhongshan page says that in 301 'the king of Zhongshan was forced to take refuge in Qi' and, in the same passage, that Zhao 'fully conquered them'; it also gives 'Conquered by Zhao: 296 BCE' and 'After ten years of war Zhao annexed them in 296', and the Wuling page says 'In 296 BC, he annexed the state of Zhongshan'. The state is therefore drawn to 296 (not 292) and the 301 refuge is a caption, not a border move. Cliopatria's 301 change is probably this passage.

wars.outcome: Zhao victory: attacks 'almost every year' from 307, several cities in 307, parts annexed in 305, the king took refuge in Qi in 301, the state annexed in 296 (295 on the Zhao page).
wars.note: Qi and Wei were asked to attack Zhongshan but 'no alliance formed' (adviser Zhang Deng); Qi's attack on Chu left Zhao free to push into Zhongshan. The page's 301 'fully conquered' conflicts with its own 296; 296 is used. The page also has Zhao invade in 306 'after the state of Zhao ... finished a military reform' (the Wuling page puts the reform and the first attack in 307).

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier. Places only: Lingshou, Dongyuan, the Great Wall built 'around 369 BC to defend itself against Zhao' (a wall about 49 km long found in Baoding in 1988), which is the one line-like feature and is not dated by a survey.

sources.title: Zhongshan (state)
sources.note: Identity, capitals, Wei conquest 407 and independence 381, 323 alliance, 315 Yan war, Zhao wars 307-296, locations. The title 'Zhongshan' in Cliopatria's Wikipedia field is the disambiguation page; this is the state article.

notes: Pages opened: the state article and the King Wuling of Zhao page (budget 1-2). START: the infobox says 'Established: 414/381'. 381 is used because the Zhongshan page has Wei conquer the state in 407 and Zhongshan 'won its independence back' in 381, and the wei dossier holds the core 407-381; a 414-407 phase under Duke Wu (capital placed at Gu, which the page does not locate) is on the page but cannot be placed, so it is not drawn. Cliopatria opens its row in 366. CLIOPATRIA SHAPES are wrong: a 10,739 km2 block north-east of Baoding that holds neither Lingshou nor Dongyuan nor the wall. The core discs are the ones the wei and zhao dossiers already use. END: 296 (Zhongshan infobox, Zhongshan text, Wuling page); the Zhao page says 295; the Zhongshan page's '301 ... fully conquered' conflicts with its own 296; Cliopatria runs to 292. NOT TERRITORIAL, left out of the ledger: 323, 'Zhongshan formed a vertical alliance' with Wei, Han, Zhao and Yan so that its ruler could style himself king (wang); the 315 invasion of Yan (copper mines, no place named; listed in wars with empty zones). NEEDS A DOSSIER: Xianyu (the page's predecessor, mentioned 506-489, a Di state); the Zhongshan Great Wall (about 369 BC, Tang County) belongs to the group's frontier-walls addition. MIRRORS: the wei dossier has the loss in 381 (counterpart zhongshan); the zhao dossier has contest_start 307, gain 305, gain 296, contest_end 296 (counterpart zhongshan); a Qi dossier line for the 301 refuge is not drawn. Rulers: none recorded; the page gives no reign dates. No area on the page, so no infobox ratio. Gazetteer: all names used (Shijiazhuang, Baoding) exist; the Lingshou disc is a coordinate because the gazetteer has no Lingshou in Hebei.
